+title: Add checkLinks, and resolve an old board name at read time with a warning
+---
+## What
+divergence.md M9 "checkLinks and repairLinks". A user must find links that use an old board name, and links that no board can resolve.
+
+## Do
+- `checkLinks(boards:)` (read only) reads the stored refs of the named boards: `dependsOn`, assignee URIs, task URLs in bodies, tombstone lines. Each link gets a class: **ok**, **old name** (with the current name), **dangling**, or **missing node**.
+- An old-name link works at read time (readiness and reads use the board that has the old name now). The response gives a warning for it.
+- `board(id:)` with an old name gives the board that has it now, with its current names.
+
+## Acceptance Criteria
+- [ ] Each of the four classes has a test.
+- [ ] A task that depends on a task through an old board name is ready when that task is done, and the response warns.
+- [ ] `board(id:)` with an old name gives the current board.
+- [ ] Tests use temporary folders and temporary git repos only.
\ No newline at end of file

+    - Plan for `checkLinks(boards:)`: a read-only `Query` field. No `boards` reads the current board. It lists one `LinkCheck` for each stored link: `dependsOn` edges, remote assignee URIs, body task URLs (`DependencyMarkers`) of live tasks, and the `Moved to <URI>` line of a tombstoned task. -- [ ] `Sources/FoundationModelsKanban/Tool/KanbanGraph.swift:716` `reuse/reuse` — addOldNameWarnings repeats the loop in addPlaceWarnings (lines 704-706): iterate a store collection, then call context.warnings.add with that item's warningMessage and warningCode. A helper that takes the collection and the code would hold this shape once. Each new warning kind would otherwise add another copy, and the copies could drift apart. Extract a private static helper, for example `addWarnings(_ items: some Sequence<...>, code: String, in context:)`, or a small generic over a warning-message protocol. Call it from addPlaceWarnings and addOldNameWarnings. Keep the per-case codes as the parameters. This is a minor duplication, so it is optional if the author prefers the explicit loops.

The change classifies old board names at read time for dependsOn links, and the same classifier reads assignee URIs. No test checks an assignee URI that holds an old board key, so the OLD_NAME class and its OLD_BOARD_NAME warning are unproven for ASSIGNEE. The same gap exists for BODY (line 274) and TOMBSTONE (line 293), which also test only the current name. Add one test in which a task assigned to a task of the related board holds the old git key, after the remote change.
